title: Memory Game
story: Simon says: remember this sequence. 3... 7... 2... now repeat it back. Each round adds one more number to the sequence. How far can your memory go before you slip? Build the game that tests working memory — and trains it.
why: A memory game teaches sequence generation, Vec for storing patterns, user input comparison, and progressively increasing difficulty — cognitive training as code.
analogy: The children's game 'Simon Says' with colored buttons that light up in sequence. Each round adds one more flash to remember. Your memory game is digital Simon: the computer plays a note, you echo it, then it plays two notes, you echo both, and the chain grows until your memory breaks.
try_it: Track the highest round reached across multiple games. Add 'display sequence' that prints numbers one by one with a delay. Add letter mode (A-H) and color mode. Implement increasing difficulty: longer sequences, shorter display time.
tips: Generate sequences using LCG — predictable but random-looking
Compare sequences element by element — early exit on first mismatch
Score = round number × multiplier — rewards longer survival
common_mistakes: Regenerating the sequence each comparison — must compare against the same target
Not checking sequence lengths first — different lengths = automatic mismatch
Using == on Vec directly instead of element-by-element comparison
